## Why visit

Rochdale’s most immediately striking pub stop, facing the town-hall square and combining a handsome traditional building with a substantial cask range. It is an easy place to make the centre of a two-pub excursion with the Baum. The kitchen and daily specials also make it a realistic food anchor. Choose an earlier visit if you want to inspect the room and discuss beer quietly, because live music and televised sport can change the atmosphere later. The visit is worthwhile for the pub, ale and food together rather than as a cider pilgrimage.

## Beer

CAMRA describes a dozen cask ales, and the official site promotes a broad real-ale range. Current beers vary. CAMRA lists Pictish-brewed Lancashire Bitter as its house cask and Phoenix, Pictish and Serious among changing breweries.

**CAMRA-listed regular beers:** Pictish — Lancashire Bitter.

**Named changing/house breweries:** Phoenix; Pictish; Serious.

## Food

Official site advertises homemade British meals and daily specials using local ingredients; CAMRA notes house-made pies.

## Plan the visit

Live music and sport can make it lively. Official opening tables conflict internally; confirm the planned visit and kitchen hours.

**Getting there:** Use Rochdale town-centre tram/bus interchange or walk into the centre from the main railway station.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
